title: Intake classification and size-based routing
summary: Before a run starts, the supervisor MUST augment the request, estimate its implementation size, record a durable classification through `pan intake classify`, and start the route that record names unless the operator overrides it.
instructions: Before `pan init`, the supervisor MUST augment the preserved request under the prompt-augmentation skill and MUST write the result to `runtime/intake/<request-stem>/augmented.md`. The original request MUST stay verbatim and remains the reference for `intake.request_covered`.

The supervisor MUST estimate the request's implementation code under the sizing handbook: SLOC, TSSRFs, modules, the horizontal layers touched, and whether it adds a new integration point. It MUST NOT estimate test code, and it MUST round SLOC up when unsure.

The supervisor MUST record the estimate with `pan intake classify --request <request> --augmented <augmented> --rationale <text>` and its estimate options before `pan init`. The supervisor MUST NOT write or edit the classification record by hand.
The supervisor's first operator report MUST show the size class, the layers touched, the integration and new-integration-point flags, the route, and the start the record names.

The supervisor MUST start the record's start: an L or XL route starts `/pan-decompose` on the augmented request, and any other route starts `pan init` with the workflow the record names. `pan intake show --request <request>` prints the exact next command.
When the operator names a workflow, that choice MUST win. The supervisor MUST record it with `--operator-workflow <workflow>` and MUST NOT reroute it.
When a route's workflow is not installed, the record falls back to `planning` and states the reason. The supervisor MUST report that fallback and MUST NOT invent a workflow.

Outside a one-shot implement stage, when a stage reports that the work exceeds its class's SLOC hard max or adds an unplanned new integration point, the supervisor MUST reclassify with `pan intake classify --reason <text>`. The supervisor MUST report the new route. Rerouting an active run stays an operator-owned stage change.

When a one-shot implement stage reports escalation (the cycle bound is exhausted, the work exceeds the S SLOC hard max, or a required decision remains unresolved), or a one-shot run pauses at its implement attempt limit, the supervisor MUST reclassify with `--reason` and MUST start the record's start. The supervisor MUST carry the latest one-shot implement output as evidence into that next run. A new integration point alone MUST NOT trigger that escalation.
